主要内容: General Electric's power unit faces significant challenges, with a 19% revenue decline and 58% profit drop in its latest quarter. Orders for new equipment fell 26% to $7.4 billion. GE expects turbine sales in 2018 to be about half of 2017 levels. The company is cutting costs, reducing its workforce, and shrinking its footprint. GE has already cut $560 million in costs in the first half of 2018, exceeding half its $1 billion target. Larry Culp, the new CEO, faces the challenge of steering GE through weak demand for its power plant equipment and addressing structural and operational issues in the power business. GE has also announced a $23 billion impairment charge related to its $10.6 billion acquisition of Alstom's power assets in 2015. The company admitted to a production issue with a blade in its next-generation HA-turbines, though a fix has been identified. Gabelli & Company noted the issue is "manageable" and would result in costs in the "hundreds of millions rather than in the billions."
